originalTitle: Flying Roadsters can’t lift Tesla’s flat Q3 revenues

content: As the smoke clears from its outrageous Roadster demo, Tesla reported Q3 earnings on Wednesday — and the cold reality is that revenue has flatlined. Tesla said it earned $1.7 billion in net income on $28.0 billion in revenue in the quarter that ended in September 2026. Revenues were flat, while profits dropped 4 percent compared to the third quarter of 2025, when the company earned $1.4 billion in net income on $28.1 billion in revenue. Tesla’s revenue came in above Wall Street expectations of $27.9 billion, according to data compiled by LSEG. Tesla’s own company-compiled expectations predicted Q3 revenues of $28.3 billion. The earnings come on the heels of a disappointing Q3 sales report, in which Tesla reported a 2.1 percent drop in customer deliveries compared to the blockbuster third quarter of 2025. (For a direct-to-consumer company like Tesla, deliveries are a proxy for sales.) The drop in sales was widely expected thanks to the expiration of the $7,500 federal tax credit for electric vehicles on September 30, 2025. Elon Musk himself said that the company was in for “a few rough quarters” thanks to the expiring incentive and other macroeconomic factors. Tesla reported automotive revenues of $20.5 billion, a 3 percent decrease year over year — a sign that the company’s car business is floundering after the elimination of the tax credit. But there were troubling signs for Tesla’s other businesses too; the company reported $2.9 billion in energy generation and storage revenue, a staggering 16 percent drop year over year. “Services and other revenue,” such as money the company takes in from EV charging, maintenance, parts, and insurance, was up 33 percent to $4.6 billion – a rare bright spot in an otherwise dour earnings report. Tesla’s capital spending — also known as capex — soared 110 percent year over year to $4.7 billion this quarter, as the company continue to pour money into AI, autonomous vehicles, and robotics. Musk has said to expect “a massive capex year” of at least $25 billion in capital spending as Tesla continues to transition into an AI and robotics company. But the company only spent $13 billion in the first three quarters of the year, suggesting that Tesla may fall short of that $25 billion target. Operating expenses — the day to day costs of running Tesla’s business — was up 39 percent year over year to $4.8 billion, while its income from operations — the profit Tesla generates from those day-to-day dealings — was down 56 percent year over year to just $718 million. On the brighter side, Tesla reported a free cash flow of $1.5 billion, after dipping into negative territory last year. Still, that figure represents a 62 percent drop year over year, a sign that Tesla’s operating revenues were still struggling to cover its capital expenditures. The possibility of a Tesla-SpaceX merger gained new momentum after Musk’s revelation this week that the two companies had formed special committees to discuss the possibility. Musk said a merger would be a “good idea,” even though he claimed he wouldn’t be involved in the process. Beyond merger talks, this past quarter also saw the highly anticipated re-reveal of the next-generation Tesla Roadster, nine years after it was initially announced. The demo in Waco, Texas, featured a redesigned two-seat prototype flying and flipping through the air using cold-gas thrusters provided by SpaceX. While the event generated its own cottage industry of online reactions, it did little to assuage skeptics that the vehicle would actually go into production in 2028, as promised.

chineseContent: 随着其令人震惊的 Roadster 演示的硝烟散去，特斯拉于周三公布了第三季度财报，而残酷的现实是收入已经持平。特斯拉表示，截至 2026 年 9 月的季度，其净利润为 17 亿美元，营收为 280 亿美元。与 2025 年第三季度相比，营收持平，而利润下降了 4%，当时该公司的净利润为 14 亿美元，营收为 281 亿美元。根据伦敦证券交易所集团 (LSEG) 编制的数据，特斯拉的收入高于华尔街预期的 279 亿美元。特斯拉自己公司编制的预期预测第三季度收入为 283 亿美元。财报发布前，特斯拉发布了令人失望的第三季度销售报告，其中特斯拉报告称，与 2025 年第三季度的表现相比，客户交付量下降了 2.1%。（对于特斯拉这样的直接面向消费者的公司来说，交付量是销量的代表。）由于 7,500 美元的电动汽车联邦税收抵免已于 2025 年 9 月 30 日到期，销量下降是人们普遍预期的结果。埃隆·马斯克本人表示，该公司将陷入困境。由于激励措施到期和其他宏观经济因素，“几个艰难的季度”。特斯拉公布的汽车收入为 205 亿美元，同比下降 3%，这表明该公司的汽车业务在取消税收抵免后陷入困境。但特斯拉的其他业务也出现了令人不安的迹象。该公司公布的能源发电和存储收入为 29 亿美元，同比下降 16%。 “服务和其他收入”，例如该公司从电动汽车充电、维护、零部件和保险中获得的收入，增长了 33%，达到 46 亿美元——这是原本黯淡的收益报告中罕见的亮点。特斯拉的资本支出——也被称为
